# Verification analysis: vlan-segmentation-ubuntu16

## Task

> `node1`, `node2`, and `node3` share a single link. Separate the two Linux
> systems onto their own VLANs over that link, `node2` on VLAN 10 and `node3` on
> VLAN 20, and route between the VLANs through `node1` so the two systems can
> still reach each other.

- Systems: **1 vyos + 2 ubuntu16.04**

- Control node: **node2**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `vlan-segmentation-ubuntu16__zHfZWNm`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor successfully segmented node2 onto VLAN 10 and node3 onto VLAN 20 across the shared link, with node1 (VyOS) routing between them via 802.1Q sub-interfaces. Direct evidence includes tcpdump proof of tagged-frame re-tagging on node1 (not flat bridging), bidirectional cross-VLAN pings, and a full pre-restart-baseline/restart/post-restart-recovery cycle on all three nodes showing configuration persists across reboot. All material task outcomes are satisfied with strong, coherent evidence.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.720 | 0.900 | 56/4 (+2 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** node2 is placed on its own 802.1Q VLAN 10 sub-interface over the shared link
  - **Why:** ens7.10 configured with 10.10.10.2/24 via VLAN 10, verified live (cmd-b1fd8e65493c4a8b) and confirmed present after actual reboot with new boot_id (cmd-fc490ae15ba94bdd, cmd-76afdd21b92c4527).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-b1fd8e65493c4a8b`, `cmd-fc490ae15ba94bdd`, `cmd-76afdd21b92c4527`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** node3 is placed on its own 802.1Q VLAN 20 sub-interface over the shared link
  - **Why:** ens7.20 configured with 10.10.20.2/24 via VLAN 20, verified live (cmd-7395a8fa87dd4c73) and confirmed present after actual reboot with new boot_id (cmd-757abd4960064803, cmd-95ff35fb34544096).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-7395a8fa87dd4c73`, `cmd-757abd4960064803`, `cmd-95ff35fb34544096`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** node1 (VyOS) routes between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 via 802.1Q sub-interfaces
  - **Why:** eth1.10 (10.10.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.1/24) configured, committed, and saved on VyOS (cmd-293841069be94819, cmd-ada88899bf784b74); ip_forward=1 confirmed both pre- and post-restart (cmd-1f93867e0ff441f1, cmd-3ffd2a62ab634959).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-293841069be94819`, `cmd-ada88899bf784b74`, `cmd-1f93867e0ff441f1`, `cmd-3ffd2a62ab634959`
- **R4 — Satisfied:** node2 and node3 can still reach each other, routed through node1 (true VLAN segmentation, not flat bridging)
  - **Why:** Bidirectional pings between 10.10.10.2 and 10.10.20.2 succeed with TTL=63 (one router hop) both before and after restarts (cmd-8e2161815f5648bd, cmd-0ccb4c39ccee4502, cmd-f044fd1707614390, cmd-76afdd21b92c4527, cmd-95ff35fb34544096); tcpdump on node1 eth1 directly shows 802.1Q-tagged frames tagged vlan 10 arriving and being re-tagged vlan 20 by node1 and vice versa, proving genuine inter-VLAN routing rather than bridging (cmd-0a89ec05388d46b5).

- **R5 — Satisfied:** Configuration persists across a reboot/restart of each managed node (VLAN interfaces, routes, and cross-VLAN connectivity recover automatically)
  - **Why:** All three nodes show a healthy pre-restart baseline with boot_id captured (cmd-c6fba7ee2da74d9d, cmd-70e66645ab41477d, cmd-a9b20a2b1c5f43b7), a restart acknowledgement and unreachability during the disruption (cmd-98895d3fdb754560/cmd-56285bac5fb048bf, cmd-6bac9718e5bd475f/cmd-6a48c2967f5a4b1b, cmd-893aad7a29f34ebc), a distinct post-restart boot_id (cmd-c447f54cedcc44aa, cmd-fc490ae15ba94bdd, cmd-757abd4960064803), and recovered VLAN interfaces, routes, ip_forward, and cross-VLAN ping (cmd-3ffd2a62ab634959, cmd-f044fd1707614390, cmd-76afdd21b92c4527, cmd-95ff35fb34544096). This is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle after_executor boot-identity snapshots matching the executor-captured post-restart boot_ids for all three nodes.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.720**. The core changes (VyOS vif config, /etc/modules and /etc/network/interfaces.d/*.cfg on the Ubuntu nodes) are correctly scoped to the task and confirmed to persist via the reboot lifecycle diffs, with no failed services, no package-health regressions, and no unrelated exposure changes in the after_executor snapshot versus after_prepare (only expected boot-id/socket-PID/tmp churn from restarts). However, node2 and node3 required an extended sequence of troubleshooting mutations to get the VLAN sub-interface address applied reliably: repeated ifdown/ifup cycles, manual `ip link del`, and several ad hoc `ip addr add`/`ip route add` commands issued outside the persisted config (cmd-8dbc9fc335614e9f, cmd-553fdc771b6a44bc, cmd-84719ffd7d14480b, cmd-a9d0e76644ac480b, cmd-fa752153d2704554, cmd-b9cd6df2018a4d49 on node2; cmd-1b83b442a19b4bd9, cmd-5dc47c87eb944e03, cmd-a64e701c29644ab9, cmd-e4d3781bf2074ea2, cmd-bb5abb819481456a on node3). These were bounded, non-destructive, and ultimately superseded by the persisted interfaces.d config, which is what was proven to survive the actual reboot -- so they left no incorrect residue, but they represent real trial-and-error against the live network state rather than clean single-shot configuration. Minor scratch files (/tmp/vlantap.log, /tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/tcpdump.pid) created for the tcpdump capture and reboot scheduling were not confirmed removed afterward, though they are low-risk and outside the bounded temp-file diff shown.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-8dbc9fc335614e9f`, `cmd-553fdc771b6a44bc`, `cmd-84719ffd7d14480b`, `cmd-fa752153d2704554`, `cmd-b9cd6df2018a4d49`, `cmd-1b83b442a19b4bd9`, `cmd-a64e701c29644ab9`, `cmd-e4d3781bf2074ea2`, `cmd-bb5abb819481456a`, `cmd-28893fd5d7804a40`, `cmd-0a89ec05388d46b5`

### Comments and limitations

- node2 and node3 VLAN configuration required multiple troubleshooting iterations (ifdown/ifup cycles, manual ip addr/route commands) before converging on the persisted interfaces.d config; the trace shows this converged correctly and was validated by an actual reboot, but the process was not clean.
- Minor scratch files (/tmp/vlantap.log, /tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/tcpdump.pid) created during evidence collection were not explicitly confirmed removed; the bounded lifecycle temp-file diff does not include them so their final disposition is indeterminate.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.720); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
